Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, The Communist Manifesto, translated by Samuel Moore.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/karl-marx_friedrich-engels/the-communist-manifesto/samuel-moore

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Karl Marx, the co-author, died 1883 (Wikidata Q9061, P570 = 1883-03-14).
- Friedrich Engels, the co-author, died 1895 (Wikidata Q34787, P570 = 1895-08-05).
- Samuel Moore, the translator, died 1911 (Wikidata Q19551496, P570 = 1911-01-01 and 1911-07-20; both dates are in 1911).

First publication of the text used: 1888 (SE colophon: 'The Communist Manifesto was published in 1848 by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels. It was translated from German in 1888 by Samuel Moore.'). The country of this translation's first publication is not stated in the facts.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1888, before 1931, so the United States public domain applies to it.
- Country of origin: the last person to die, Samuel Moore, died in 1911. Every person whose words are in the text died in 1925 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less, whatever the country of first publication.
